back: A compound that contains hydrogen and carbon only.
notes: Ethanol is not a hydrocarbon: it contains oxygen.

back: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, and similar chemical properties.
notes: Supplement: successive members differ by CH₂ and show a trend in physical properties.

back: The atom or group of atoms that decides the chemical properties of a homologous series.
notes: Examples: C=C in alkenes, –OH in alcohols, –COOH in carboxylic acids.

back: Saturated: only single C–C bonds (alkanes). Unsaturated: at least one C=C double bond (alkenes).

front: General formulae of the four homologous series
notes: In the carboxylic acid formula, n does not count the carbon of –COOH.

back: Every atom and every bond in the molecule (including the O–H bond).
notes: C has 4 bonds, O has 2, H has 1.

back: How the atoms are arranged, unambiguously, without drawing every bond, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2OH}$.
notes: Supplement wording: it shows unambiguously how the atoms are arranged.

front: Five characteristics of a homologous series
back: Same functional group; same general formula; differ by CH₂; trend in physical properties; similar chemical properties.

front: Name endings of the four series
How does boiling point change along a homologous series?
back: It increases as the chain gets longer: bigger molecules have stronger forces between them.
